answer: Deferred identity drawdown. Each new agent identity must first route a small fixed task through the shared kernel before it can transact; the result is withheld until a comet-like release schedule returns it over many epochs, reaching nadir only after full dilution. If the operator abandons or duplicates identities, all pending outputs for that operator are voided, not just the offending wallet. Attacker cost: each identity ties up a full task's compute and forfeits it on any sybil cluster detection, so mass registration loses capital proportional to cluster size.
